study_identification.title: Molecular and micro-architectural mapping of gray matter alterations in psychosis

study_characteristics.study_objective: To characterize the molecular and micro-architectural attributes that underlie the pattern of cortical atypical maturation in different psychosis-related groups.

dataset_name.answer: ABCD, ASRB, B-SNIP, CNP, MCIC, UKB, PAFIP, ALSPAC

hc_age.answer: 51.91 ± 23.68 (9.76, 81.82) for the main HC group. Other HC groups are mentioned for specific comparisons.

hc_sex.answer: 19,139 F in the main HC group.

quality_checking_detail.answer: Thirteen HC subjects exhibiting significant artifacts or processing errors were excluded from further analysis. Sensitivity analyses were conducted using the Euler index as a proxy for image quality to evaluate the stability of centile estimations.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: A generalized additive model for location, scale, and shape (GAMLSS) was used to estimate cross-sectional normative age-related trends from 100 different studies, which accounts for site-effects.

model_origin_detail.answer: The model, available at https://github.com/brainchart/Lifespan, estimated cross-sectional normative age-related trends from 100 different studies (around 120,000 participants; see Supplementary Information in [20] for details of the normative cohort, pages 120-151).

predictor_effects.answer: Age-normed and sex-stratified measures of brain structure atypicalities across the lifespan, known as centiles, could be derived for each psychosis-related and HC individual in our cohorts. The out-of-sample data is aligned to the corresponding epoch of the normative trajectory, using maximum likelihood to estimate the study specific offsets (random effects) for three moments of the underlying statistical distributions: mean (μ), variance (σ), and skewness (ν) in an age- and sex-specific manner.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The normative model used (GAMLSS from BrainChart) explicitly models and accounts for nuisance variables like age, sex, and site. The paper states "a centile method that removes age-, sex-, and site-effects".
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Using a centile method that removes age-, sex-, and site-effects [40], we were able to detect brain volume deviations from the expected trajectories.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper does not describe any validation of the normative model on a non-independent subset of the training data. The model is pre-trained.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study applies a pre-trained normative model to new, independent datasets. The paper mentions leave-one-study-out cross-validation.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: Leave-one-study-out cross-validation performed both within the chronic group and SCZ diagnosis indicated that centiles and loadings were not primarily in/uenced by individual studies (Supplementary Figs. 12 and 13, respectively).
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.location: Page 7, "Mapping neurobiological maps to centiles" section.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study does not appear to validate the model on a dataset from a different domain (e.g., a different modality or population not related to psychosis).

clinical_dataset.answer: ABCD, ASRB, B-SNIP, CNP, MCIC, UKB, PAFIP, ALSPAC

diseases_studied.answer: Schizophrenia (SCZ); Schizoaffective disorder (SAD); First episode of psychosis (FEP); Psychotic experiences (PE); First-degree relatives of schizophrenia (SCZ-relatives); First-degree relatives of schizoaffective disorder (SAD-relatives)

clinical_groups_n.answer: SCZ: 525, SAD: 62, FEP: 352, PE-suspected: 48, PE-definite: 73, PE-clinical: 36, SCZ-relatives: 96, SAD-relatives: 64

clinical_groups_sex.answer: SCZ: 148 F, SAD: 37 F, FEP: 138 F, PE-suspected: 33 F, PE-definite: 42 F, PE-clinical: 28 F, SCZ-relatives: 68 F, SAD-relatives: 43 F

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Wilcoxon rank-sum test, Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction, Cohen's d, Sum of Squared Differences (SSD), permutation test, PCA-CCA, spin test, Pearson correlation.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study identified group-specific volume deviations below the expected trajectory for different psychosis-related conditions based on centiles and revealed an overlapping spatial distribution of the neurobiological features, which were highly colocalized with the abnormal GM trajectories.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study used a normative modeling approach on a large dataset (38,696 HC, 1256 psychosis-related cases) to generate centile scores for cortical GM phenotypes. It found significant GM volume reductions in all psychosis-related groups, with more severe effects in clinically diagnosed patients (FEP and chronic SCZ/SAD). These reductions were spatially correlated with neurobiological features, particularly metabolism (CMRGlu, CBF) and neurotransmitter concentrations (5-HT, α4β2 receptors). The findings suggest that these neurobiological features contribute to the vulnerability of specific brain regions to atypical maturation in psychosis.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: 1) Heterogeneous grouping of psychotic disorders. 2) Potential influence of antipsychotic medication on chronic individuals. 3) Normative models were only available for cortical brain volume averaged across hemispheres. 4) Risk of overfitting with CCA, though mitigated by PCA and PLS. 5) Neurobiological data were from non-psychotic individuals. 6) Loadings, not weights, were reported from the PCA-CCA model.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The findings could help define subtypes for future imaging-first molecular phenotyping.

general_notes.general_notes: The study provides a comprehensive mapping of neurobiological features to structural brain alterations in psychosis, supporting the regional vulnerability hypothesis. The use of a large-scale normative model and a wide range of psychosis-related conditions are major strengths.
